newsitem.title: USA: Ford Dec. U.S. vehicle sales up 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Ford Dec. U.S. vehicle sales up 10 pct.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. said its December U.S. vehicle sales rose 10 percent over a year earlier, with a 1 percent increase in car sales and an 18 percent increase in truck sales.
Ford has not yet released actual sales totals for the month of December, but announced the percentage increases at a news conference at the Detroit auto show Monday.
However, Ford said its total U.S. truck sales for 1996 were 2,150,575 units, an increase of 84,542 units over 1995.

The automaker's Taurus mid-size sedan also retained its status as the best selling car in the United States during 1996 for the fifth year in a row, with sales totaling 401,049 units, an increase of nine percent over 1995. The nearest passenger car competitor was Honda Motor Co. Ltd's Accord, which recorded sales of 382,298 units.
Ford Division general manager Ross Roberts said he expects a closer race for the best selling car next year with the Accord.
Roberts, speaking to reporters, said he expects Taurus sales for 1997 to fall to 380,000 to 390,000 units.
He said much of the outcome of this year's contest will depend on how many Accords Honda can produce in the United States and how many it chooses to import from Japan.
"It will be close. We're not going to by any means give it to them," Roberts said.
However, he said in 1997, the Ford Division plans to focus on boosting sales of its entire lineup of vehicles. "I'd rather have five of the top 10 than the number one selling car," he said.
Roberts added that the $1,000 rebate on the Taurus is not expected to change in the first quarter of 1997.
